title: Development of a Correlative Imaging Pipeline Bringing Together Cryogenic Soft X-ray and Electron Tomography
content: Biomedical imaging approaches have recently experienced a renaissance. The single particle cryo electron microscopy (cryoEM) field had a “resolution revolution”, the volume electron microscopy (vEM) field had a “quiet revolution”, and while it hasn’t received a similarly a catchy title, the X-ray imaging field has seen advances in both high resolution and wide field of view in recent years [1-5]. While these fields are divided by the nuances associated with the sample preparation, imaging technique and data reconstruction process, they are unified in their generation of captivating visual depictions of biomedical structures, events and processes across cellular and tissue length scales. There is also commonality in the need to annotate, visualise, and derive information from these complex, three-dimensional representations of biomedical processes. And finally, there is a need for additional commonality to develop joined-up workflows to enable routine correlative approaches tailored to the requirements of the biomedical question of interest.
